questions.q: How did the outbreak of war change Gbowee's plans after she graduated at 17?
a: Her family fled to Ghana and university became a distant dream
She joined the rebels to fight the government
She moved abroad to finish her medical degree
She took a job in the president's government
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes her family becoming refugees and her dream of becoming a doctor slipping away.

questions.q: What did Liberia look like within weeks of the rebellion starting?
a: Daily street executions, no electricity and little food
A calm capital with soldiers keeping public order
A thriving economy supported by foreign aid
A country split into two peaceful regions
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the country spun into chaos, with executions, power cuts and scarce food.

questions.q: What work did Gbowee find while studying for her social work degree?
a: Helping war survivors and former child soldiers heal
Teaching medicine at the national university
Running a refugee shelter in Nigeria
Organizing peace talks for the interim government
questions.why: Lesson 2 says she volunteered at a trauma healing program, which later became a paid job.

questions.q: How did Gbowee come to lead the first Liberian chapter of WIPNET?
a: A Nigerian woman she met at a conference appointed her
She was elected by the women of her neighborhood
The interim government hired her for the role
She founded the network herself after the war
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Thelma Ekiyor put her in charge of the new network's first chapter.

questions.q: What did Gbowee and the WIPNET women do when the peace talks kept stalling?
a: They blockaded the negotiation room until talks moved forward
They marched on the president's house and occupied it
They called a national strike by all public workers
They took the rebel leaders to court in Ghana
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes them locking delegates inside the conference room until progress was made.
